subject: Intermediary commissioning model + velocity-trigger discounts for marketplace private offer
body:
From: Kate Raymond <kate@lumenhealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: partner@medresell.io
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace private offer — reseller commission mechanics and velocity triggers

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement had a few clarifying questions as we draft the internal MA plan for the GCP marketplace private offer:

- How will reseller commissions to MedResell be handled operationally? Will that be a pass-through from the public list price (i.e., a lower invoice amount to us), or will Redwood pay a separate rebate/commission to the partner so our list/PO amounts match what’s in our budget?
- We need a clear waterfall showing list price, Redwood discount, marketplace fee, and any intermediary commission so we can map to our internal cost center. Can you share an example spreadsheet?
- We are evaluating velocity-trigger discounts (e.g., if billed spend in a quarter exceeds $X, apply an additional discount for the remainder of the quarter). What's your recommended approach and do you support retroactive true-ups?

Attached is the RFP excerpt for context. Happy to hop on a quick call but would prefer the waterfall and a short summary first.

Regards,
Kate Raymond
Director, Procurement — Lumen Health
Kate.Raymond@lumenhealth.com

-----Original Message-----

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Kate Raymond <kate@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Marketplace private offer — reseller commission mechanics and velocity triggers

Hi Kate — great questions and thanks for the RFP extract. I pulled together an initial waterfall and a few operational notes:

1) Commission handling: Redwood recommends paying the reseller (MedResell) a partner rebate out of a partner pool rather than reducing your invoiced list price. That keeps your PO/list price intact for internal accounting and preserves marketplace reporting. Practically this means: Redwood issues full invoice to Lumen Health at private-offer list price + Redwood discount; Redwood pays MedResell a quarterly rebate based on agreed tiers.

2) Waterfall: attached is a short spreadsheet that maps list price -> Redwood discount -> marketplace fee (GCP percentage) -> partner rebate. The partner rebate is documented as a separate line item in our internal settlement and does not affect the invoice amount you receive.

3) Velocity triggers & true-ups: we support quarterly true-ups. Proposal:
  - Tier 1: $0 – $500k quarterly billings: 3% partner rebate
  - Tier 2: $500k – $1.5M quarterly billings: 5% partner rebate
  - Tier 3: > $1.5M quarterly billings: 7% partner rebate
Retroactive true-up: If a quarterly threshold is hit after month 2, we do a single true-up payment to MedResell at quarter close.

Notes / asks: Can you confirm whether Lumen will require partner commissions to be visible on your GL (we can itemize in a separate settlement report) and whether a quarterly cadence works for you? Looping Ben for the commercial attachment and Olga for finance/legal on invoicing/tax.

Thanks — attaching proposed-waterfall.xlsx 

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

Attachments:
- proposed-waterfall.xlsx (xlsx)

-----Original Message-----

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kate Raymond <kate@lumenhealth.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Marketplace private offer — reseller commission mechanics and velocity triggers

Kate — thanks for the clear questions. A couple additional commercial clarifications from pricing:  

- Private offer anchoring: for GCP private offers we map your committed unit prices to a private-offer SKU. The list price shows on the invoice but the internal mapping applies your committed discount. Keeping the commission outside the invoice delivers cleaner accounting for customers and reduces risk of misallocated credits.
- Commission caps: Redwood is comfortable with a partner rebate approach, but we propose capping the partner rebate at 6% net effective for the first 12 months to preserve unit economics while still enabling partner motion. The tiered waterfall Mina proposed can be front-loaded (higher partner rebate in Q1) only if Lumen takes a minimum committed spend of $1.25M over the first 3 months. 
- True-up mechanics: quarterly true-ups paid to MedResell within 45 days of quarter close; Redwood will provide a settlement report with invoice references and usage exports as evidence.

I'm dropping the DocuSign private-offer template here for sign-off. If procurement wants to front-load discounts (e.g., 8% in Q1), we need a corresponding committed spend schedule in the MA plan.

Link: https://docusign.net/link/AA12BB34

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

-----Original Message-----

From: Kate Raymond <kate@lumenhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: partner@medresell.io
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Marketplace private offer — reseller commission mechanics and velocity triggers

Ben / Mina — quick follow-ups from procurement: 

1) The 6% cap is reasonable but we need clarity on the threshold that moves an account from Tier 1 to Tier 2. For example, if spend is $480k in Q1 and we hit $520k in month 2, does the quarter get upgraded to Tier 2 and apply retroactively? Your note suggested yes but need formal wording.
2) Can you confirm true-up cadence and payment terms? Quarterly true-up within 45 days works for our banks but we need a clear definition of the measurement window and confirmation that you’ll provide the usage exports we can reconcile against GCP billing.
3) Front-loading: we would prefer a modest front-load (8% partner rebate in Q1) to help MedResell ramp. If you require a $1.25M 90-day commit for that, provide the simplest language we can include in the MA plan so our internal finance can greenlight.

I can share a short clause if you want but would prefer to see Redwood's draft wording on all three.

Thanks,
Kate

-----Original Message-----

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Kate Raymond <kate@lumenhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Marketplace private offer — reseller commission mechanics and velocity triggers

Hi Kate — copying in legal/finance language that we typically use. Summary below and attached a draft clause: commission-terms-draft.docx.

Operational summary (short):
- Commission / partner rebate mechanic: Redwood will issue invoices to Lumen Health at agreed private-offer list price and applicable customer discount. Partner commissions will be paid as a separate quarterly rebate to MedResell based on agreed tiers and documented in Redwood’s partner settlement. Commissions will not reduce the invoiced amount to the customer.
- Tier upgrade & retroactivity: If the quarterly aggregated billable spend crosses a higher tier at quarter close, Redwood will calculate a single retroactive true-up payment to MedResell for the entire quarter at the higher tier rate. Example language included in the attached docx.
- True-up cadence and evidence: Quarterly true-ups; payments made within 45 days of quarter close. Redwood will provide usage exports and an invoice reference file. Lumen Health and MedResell will have a 60-day audit window from rebate payment date to request supporting records.
- Front-loaded commissions: We will accept a one-time front-load to Tier 2 (8%) for Q1 only if an irrevocable 90-day commitment of $1.25M is accepted by Lumen Health and documented in the MA plan. The attached draft includes a simple schedule clause and remedies for shortfall (pro-rated clawback of excess rebate).
- Tax & invoicing: Commissions paid as rebates; Redwood will supply an aggregate settlement report to enable your GL mapping. Any VAT/sales tax treatment will follow the tax law in the invoice jurisdiction; Redwood will net against partner settlement where applicable.

Attached: commission-terms-draft.docx

If that language looks good I can route a short DocuSign amendment for signature.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Director, Finance & Commercial Legal — Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com

Attachments:
- commission-terms-draft.docx (docx)

Thanks all — that draft is exactly what we needed. Quarterly true-ups and the 60-day audit window are fine. We’ll accept the one-time front-load to 8% in Q1 provided the $1.25M 90-day commitment is in the MA plan; I’ll send procurement’s clause in a separate email this afternoon to make sure wording matches.

Please proceed with the DocuSign amendment and attach the proposed-waterfall.xlsx and commission draft. CC’ing MedResell to confirm they’re aligned with the settlement timing.

Best,
Kate Raymond
